Most participants identified as women (n = 88, 82.24%) and White (n = 99, 92.52%). On average, participants were 39.87 (SD = 13.35) years old and had a BMI of 35.10 (SD = 8.67). Further, participants generally reported LOC eating at a moderate level of severity across the assessed dimensions, yet with high variability (all ranges = 1-5): (1) general feeling of losing control while eating (M = 2.26, SD = 1.32); (2) difficulties resisting eating (M = 2.79, SD = 1.42); (3) difficulties stopping eating after starting (M = 2.54, SD = 1.41); (4) feeling driven or compelled to eat (M = 2.88, SD = 1.38); (5) not paying attention to one's eating (M = 3.45, SD = 1.18); (6) feeling disconnected while eating (M = 2.19, SD = 1.26). Further, a prior analysis of the present sample examined whether the momentary negative affect-binge eating association was mediated by negative urgency (i.e., a self-regulatory process that overlaps with emotion dysregulation [r = 0.948 in the present study] and is defined as behaving impulsively while experiencing negative affect; Wonderlich et al. [2024]). Regarding the direct effects, across models, there were significant positive associations between the negative affect and emotion dysregulation latent factors at the within-person (b = 0.24) and between-person (b = 0.90) levels, and inverse associations between the positive affect and emotion dysregulation factors at the within-person (b = -0.08) but not between-person level. consequence.explanation: The mediation effect for 'difficulties resisting eating' (p = .026) does not survive any of the four corrections, yet it is named in the abstract and conclusions as one of the dimensions emotion dysregulation was found to mediate.

findings.notes: Twelve mediation tests on the same 107 participants, testing one hypothesis across six correlated outcomes, with no correction stated anywhere. This is an ordinary reporting practice, not misconduct - but the arithmetic is that the family-wise error rate reaches 46% and roughly 0.6 false positives are expected by chance. Three of the four uncorrected claims are robust (all p = .001, surviving even Bonferroni); the fourth, difficulties resisting eating at p = .026, exceeds every threshold (Bonferroni .0042, BH .0125, BY .0040). The surviving-claims interval is 3 to 3, i.e. all four methods agree. Note the six LOC outcomes are measured on the same subjects and are plainly correlated, so Benjamini-Yekutieli is the appropriate FDR method here, and it too keeps only 3.

findings.notes: READ THE CAVEAT BEFORE USING THIS. The derived interval excludes zero, which superficially contradicts the reported p = .065 - but that is a ROUNDING ARTIFACT, not a defect in the paper. b and SE are printed to 2 dp, so b = -0.02, SE = 0.01 taken at their midpoints gives z = -2.0; the true unrounded values (e.g. b = -0.018, SE = 0.0098) reconcile with p = .065 comfortably. check_regression_batch confirmed this row consistent, with a reachable p-interval of [6e-07, 0.317]. The reportable observation is different and softer: three of the six within-person positive-affect mediation paths sit at p = .065-.070, all just above threshold, so the paper's flat conclusion that positive-affect pathways 'were not significant' rests on marginal rather than clearly null evidence, and no confidence intervals are printed anywhere that would let a reader see this.

consequence.explanation: The headline conclusion that positive-affect mediation was uniformly absent is carried by three marginal results (p = .065, .067, .070), not by clearly null ones - a weaker basis than the flat statement suggests.

findings.notes: READ THE CAVEAT BEFORE USING THIS. The derived interval excludes zero, which superficially contradicts the reported p = .065 - but that is a ROUNDING ARTIFACT, not a defect in the paper. b and SE are printed to 2 dp, so b = -0.02, SE = 0.01 taken at their midpoints gives z = -2.0; the true unrounded values (e.g. b = -0.018, SE = 0.0098) reconcile with p = .065 comfortably. check_regression_batch confirmed this row consistent, with a reachable p-interval of [6e-07, 0.317]. There is therefore NO internal contradiction, and none should be reported. The reportable observation is softer: three of the six within-person positive-affect mediation paths sit at p = .065-.070, all just above threshold, so the flat conclusion that positive-affect pathways 'were not significant' rests on marginal rather than clearly null evidence - and no confidence intervals are printed anywhere that would let a reader see this.
